incident.title: Payment timeouts spiking
incident.teaser: Looks like the deploy, but the timeouts started before it
incident.description: Alert: payment timeouts above threshold; unpaid orders piling up. The v1.4.2 deploy went out at 14:10 UTC and the log format changed at the same time.

steps.reasoning: Payment timeouts reportedly began around the 14:10 deploy, but we haven't checked whether they actually started before or after it. Metrics should confirm the timing first.
steps.task: When did payment timeout rates and payment latency start rising relative to the v1.4.2 deploy at 2026-11-12T14:10:00Z? Report the onset time, how steep the rise was, and any other changes around then (traffic, payment provider latency, config changes). Use metrics, because the log format changed at 14:10 and log counts may not compare across that point.

steps.reasoning: Timeouts rose at 13:50, 20 minutes before the 14:10 deploy, and plateaued with no step at the deploy. This matches PayFast's reported us-east degradation since 13:50, so the cause is the external provider, not v1.4.2.

N1 2026-11-12T14:02:00Z [vendor status page] PayFast: degraded performance in us-east. Elevated API latency and timeouts since 13:50 UTC. Investigating.
N2 2026-11-12T14:26:00Z [on-call chat] Logs look different since the deploy (JSON now). Did the deploy break payments?

submitted.summary: Payment timeouts started rising in the 13:50–13:59 bucket, about 20 minutes before the v1.4.2 deploy at 14:10. They jumped sharply, from 0.16 to 2.73/min (about 17x), reached a plateau of about 3.57/min at 14:00–14:09, and stayed flat after the deploy. The timing matches PayFast's report of degraded us-east service since 13:50, so the deploy and the log-format change are unlikely to be the cause. No payment-latency metric exists, so I couldn't measure latency directly.

evidence.detail: Timeouts were 0.14–0.16/min through 13:49, rose to 2.73 at 13:50–13:59 and 3.57 at 14:00–14:09, then held at 3.40–3.59 after 14:10, with no step at the deploy.
Error rate followed the same pattern: 0.12% at 13:40–13:49, 2.26% at 13:50–13:59 and 2.83% at 14:00–14:09, then 2.71–2.93% after the deploy, so the rise came before 14:10.
PayFast's status page (14:02) reports higher API latency and timeouts in us-east since 13:50 UTC, the same bucket where our metrics rise.
Traffic stayed flat at about 19.5–20.3/min throughout, so a traffic surge is ruled out.
Average order value stayed flat at about $73–75, so there was no change in order mix.
The deploy at 14:10 came after the onset at 13:50 and produced no further step in any metric. No config-change record or payment-latency metric is available to check.

report.root_cause: Payment timeouts began rising at 13:50 UTC, about 20 minutes before the v1.4.2 deploy, and match PayFast's reported us-east API latency and timeout degradation since 13:50. The most likely cause is the external payment provider (PayFast) degradation, not our deploy. Timeouts plateaued at 14:00–14:09 and showed no additional step at 14:10.
ruled_out: The v1.4.2 deploy is ruled out as the trigger because timeouts and error rate rose at 13:50, before the 14:10 deploy, with no further step afterward.
The log-format change is ruled out as an artifact because the rise appears in metrics, not just log counts, and predates 14:10.
A traffic surge is ruled out because orders per minute stayed flat at about 19.5–20.3/min.
A change in order mix is ruled out because average order value stayed flat at about $73–75.
report.suggested_fix: Treat this as a PayFast us-east incident: track the provider status, consider failover to another region or provider or extended retry/backoff if available, and reconcile unpaid orders once PayFast recovers. No rollback of v1.4.2 is indicated, though config changes could not be checked because no record was available.

verdictReason: The evidence points away from the deploy, and no test showed a regression.
